rootCauses.summary: The village:entered listener starts the optional enhancement loader immediately from the entry click lifecycle, so the browser can begin heavy evaluation before a clean first playable paint.
rootCauses.prediction: The entry click gets a paint boundary before optional enhancement evaluation begins.
rootCauses.falsifier: Source/native evidence still starts enhancement import before the paint boundary.

rootCauses.summary: mura-enhancements statically imports the whole ordered side-effect graph, allowing multiple expensive modules to evaluate as one uninterrupted post-entry task.
rootCauses.prediction: The same ordered modules load through sequential dynamic imports with a browser-turn yield between each module.
rootCauses.falsifier: Enhancements are reordered/removed, or the graph still evaluates through top-level static imports without yields.

rootCauses.summary: Character runtime integration and village visual language are loaded immediately after the enhancement graph with no scheduling boundary.
rootCauses.prediction: Those final presentation stages retain order but yield between stages.
rootCauses.falsifier: Final presentation stages are reordered or still execute back-to-back in the same cooperative chain.

observation.summary: After the prior title-screen deferral, immutable staging now makes the title responsive, but clicking 村へ入る produces repeated 1.2–2.1s long tasks during the first playable seconds. The remaining problem moved from pre-entry to post-entry rather than disappearing.

conditions.scenario: title -> 村へ入る -> 5s first playable dwell

notVerified: which individual enhancement module dominates each long task

evidence.statement: The entered event immediately begins the enhancement import chain and then loads character runtime and visual language back-to-back.
The post-entry enhancement graph is a sequence of static side-effect imports, so module evaluation is not cooperatively yielded between stages.

evidence.symbol: title entry is a lifecycle boundary before post-entry enhancement loading
evidence.statement: Existing regression protects the entry/enhancement lifecycle boundary but does not require a playable-frame/yield boundary inside post-entry loading.

hypothesis.cause: Heavy post-entry work was moved behind player intent, but it still executes as a largely monolithic ordered graph immediately after the click, blocking the first playable interaction window.
hypothesis.prediction: A paint boundary before loading plus ordered per-module browser-turn yields will preserve every enhancement while eliminating the monolithic post-entry critical section.
hypothesis.falsifier: Focused assertions cannot prove ordering/yields, enhancements fail to become ready, or same-condition staging still shows equivalent multi-second uninterrupted entry stalls.

candidates.reason: Preserves every existing enhancement and semantic order while giving rendering/input a scheduling opportunity between expensive stages.
requestIdleCallback-only loading can starve indefinitely under continuous animation and would make feature readiness timing unpredictable.
Would weaken established gameplay/presentation quality rather than fixing scheduling.

implementation.summary: Add a first-paint boundary after entry, replace the monolithic static enhancement graph with ordered dynamic imports that yield between modules, and preserve final presentation ordering with explicit browser-turn yields.

limitations: Hosted Chromium/SwiftShader timing is directional rather than physical-device performance.
Native assertion proves scheduling structure and order, not absolute milliseconds.
